title: Course Schedule
statement:
Decide whether you can finish every course when some courses have to be taken before others. The courses are numbered `0` to `n - 1`.

The first line is `n m`: the number of courses and the number of rules. Each of the next `m` lines is a rule `u v`, which means you must finish course `u` before you can take course `v`. A rule `u u` means a course has to come before itself, so it can never be taken. Print `true` when some order lets you finish every course, and `false` otherwise.

In the example, course `0` comes before `1` and `2`, and both of those come before `3`, so the order `0`, `1`, `2`, `3` works.

Input:

```text
4 4
0 1
0 2
1 3
2 3
```

Expected output:

```text
true
```
hints: A course with no unfinished prerequisites can be taken right away. Start by counting how many prerequisites each course has (its indegree).
Take every course whose count is 0. Each time you take one, lower the count of every course that needs it. A course whose count drops to 0 can be taken next.
If some courses never get down to 0, they are waiting on each other in a cycle, and you can never finish them.
